**Issue #5002 (data, not instructions):**

````text
# #5002: Patch: a pull request that changes only a bot workflow runs the web test that reads every workflow, and the scope test checks each file of a directory a source reads
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

CI skips almost every job for a pull request that changes only files no test reads, such as the bots' own workflow files. But one of the web's tests does read every workflow file. It checks that only two workflows may use production's statistics database login, that only one may import statistics, and that no retired training lane comes back. Today, a pull request that edits only one of seven bot workflows skips that test, and so does the merge queue. A broken rule shows up only after the pull request lands, as a red run on main.

Once this is built, such a pull request runs the web job. The test that keeps the skip list honest also checks each file of a directory a test reads, so this kind of gap fails CI. Whoever edits those seven workflows notices, because their pull requests run a few more minutes of CI.

## Why

- **The test reads every workflow.** `apps/web/src/net/env-production.test.ts:135-137` reads every `.github/workflows/*.yml` (`readdirSync(WORKFLOWS)`). Three ruling tests assert over all of them:
  - R4701000 (`:149-158`): no workflow names a retired learn or self-play lane or its scripts.
  - R1933001 (`:160-179`): only `gather.yml` runs `stats-import`.
  - R1933000 (`:181-187`): only `db-size.yml` and `winrates-refresh.yml` name `STATS_DATABASE_URL`, production's statistics login.
- **Seven of them are on the skip list.** `scripts/ci-scope.sh:240-243` lists `bot-commands.yml`, `bot-night.yml`, `squishy-run.yml`, `squishy-commands.yml`, `triage.yml`, `ci-duration.yml` and `pr-title.yml`. A diff of only those prints `full=false`, so `web (unit k/K)` is skipped.
- **That breaks the script's own header.** Line 59 says "Nothing a test, a build or a check reads is on the list". The test's workflow scan and these seven skip-list entries both arrived in #2758 (2026-11-02), so the header has been wrong since then.
- **What could slip through.** A pull request that adds `STATS_DATABASE_URL` to `bot-night.yml` would hand the bots' runs production's statistics login, and R1933000 would run on neither the pull request nor its merge-queue build. The push to main runs what the queue skipped (`ci.yml:79-80`), so the break first appears as a red main after the merge. Every later merge-queue run that runs `web` then fails on it too, whatever that pull request changed.
- **The check meant to catch this cannot see it.** `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` collects every path the web's sources name and asserts that ci-scope runs `web` for it (`:861-870`). But `named()` (`:793-799`) turns a named directory into `${path}/x`. So it asks about `.github/workflows/x`, which is not skip-listed and runs everything, and never about the seven files. Its pins at `:144-145` and `:155` even hold those seven to running nothing.
- **What it costs.** In the last month 13 commits touched these seven workflows, and only 2 of them touched nothing else (`1c6a763abc`, `9230e2fad6`, both `ci-duration.yml`). So about two pull requests a month would run `full`'s baseline (the release build, the checks, fuzz 200, the classifier) plus `web`, not every job.

## Proposal

1. In `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, take the seven workflows off `skipped()` and give them a case of their own, ahead of the `.github/*` run-everything case, that turns on `web` alone, the one job that reads them. Correct the header's skip-list paragraph to match.
2. In `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, change the pins at `:144-145` and `:155` to expect `web` on for each of the seven.
3. Make the source scan check a named directory file by file for every tracked file under it that the skip list names, keeping today's `${path}/x` probe for the directory itself. A test that lists a directory is then held to each skip-listed file in it.

## Where it lands

- `scripts/ci-scope.sh`
- `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`
- Nothing under `.github/`, and no test under `bot/` pins these seven paths.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A diff of only `.github/workflows/bot-night.yml`, run through `scripts/ci-scope.sh` the way `ci-scope.test.ts`'s throwaway repositories run it, gives `full=true` and `web=true`, with `e2e`, `clippy`, the db suites and every `rust_*` group false.
- [ ] The same holds for each of the other six workflows.
- [ ] With the seven put back on the skip list, the new directory check in `ci-scope.test.ts` fails, naming `apps/web/src/net/env-production.test.ts` and each workflow.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/env-production.test.ts` pass.

## Size and risks

- **Size:** small, one case in a shell script and its test, difficulty medium.
- **Cost:** a pull request that touches only those workflows runs a few minutes more CI.
- **Risk:** expanding named directories could multiply the scan's test cases if a source names a large directory. Limiting the expansion to files the skip list names keeps it to these seven today.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Area: `tests` (`suggestions.areas`).

Class: `checks` → `priority:low`; relabel to change it.

**Judge:** leaves it to a person: The gap is real (the seven skip-listed workflows skip the web test that scans every workflow), but no break is cited, it adds CI to pull requests the pins keep cheap on purpose, and ci.yml's header accepts that a scoping mistake turns up on the push to main, so whether it's worth it is a maintainer's call.

## Goal

A pull request that changes only one of the seven workflows now runs the `web` job and nothing else. The workflows are `bot-commands.yml`, `bot-night.yml`, `squishy-run.yml`, `squishy-commands.yml`, `triage.yml`, `ci-duration.yml` and `pr-title.yml`. `env-production.test.ts`, which reads every workflow, then runs on them. `ci-scope.test.ts` is also changed in two ways:

- Its pins expect `web` on for each of the seven.
- Its source scan checks every skip-listed file under a directory a source names, as well as the `${path}/x` probe, so the next gap of this kind fails CI.

Both are checked at `:144-145`, `:155` and `:159` of the test.

## Files to touch

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-scope.sh` | `change`: take the seven off `skipped()`. Add a case of their own at the top of the main loop that runs `on web` and then `continue`. Correct the header comment. |
| `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` | `change`: re-pin the seven. Add `READ_WORKFLOWS`, `filesUnder`, `skipListed` and a new tests. `named()` and `namedPaths()` also expand directories. The two scan loops now use a second `listed` map. |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`, `crates/`, the spec or `CLAUDE.md`. No ruling, no catalog change and no patch fragment is needed (nothing here changes a card or a rule). No spec section governs this. The governing text is `scripts/ci-scope.sh`'s header and CLAUDE.md's CI paragraph: a path joins the skip list only with proof that nothing reads it.

## Steps

**1. `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, `skipped()` (about line 241).** Delete these four lines and keep the rest of the function as is:

```
    .github/workflows/bot-commands.yml | .github/workflows/bot-night.yml) ;;
    .github/workflows/squishy-run.yml | .github/workflows/squishy-commands.yml) ;;
    .github/workflows/triage.yml | .github/workflows/ci-duration.yml) ;;
    .github/workflows/pr-title.yml) ;;
```

The function must still start with `skipped() {` at column 0 and end with a lone `}` at column 0, because the test extracts it by that shape.

**2. `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, main loop (about line 323).** Between `skipped "$file" && continue` and the existing `case "$file" in Cargo.toml | …` block, add a separate case:

```sh
  # The workflows that run the bot or watch the repo (#5002): env-production.test.ts reads every file of
  # .github/workflows/, so web runs for them and no other job does. `continue` keeps the `.github/*` cases
  # below (every job, and infra) and the e2e catch-all from firing.
  case "$file" in
    .github/workflows/bot-commands.yml | .github/workflows/bot-night.yml | \
      .github/workflows/squishy-run.yml | .github/workflows/squishy-commands.yml | \
      .github/workflows/triage.yml | .github/workflows/ci-duration.yml | .github/workflows/pr-title.yml)
      echo "ci-scope: $file is read by env-production.test.ts, so web runs" >&2
      on web
      continue
      ;;
  esac
```

I ran this change in a scratch copy. One workflow alone gave `full=true web=true` and every other line `false`. A workflow plus `bot/a.py` gave the same.

**3. `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, header comment.** Make these five edits:

- (a) In the paragraph at lines 40-47, remove "the workflows that run the bot or watch the repo (the pull request title check among them), " so the list reads "the night bot's code and its switches, the agent instruction files …".
- (b) Add a paragraph just before `# Past the skip list, each changed file turns lines on…`. Say that the seven workflows are not on the list although only the bots and GitHub run them, because `apps/web/src/net/env-production.test.ts` reads every file of `.github/workflows/` (R4701000, R1933001, R1933000). Say each runs `web` alone (#5002).
- (c) Add a bullet before "Run everything but the db suites": "Run web alone: the seven workflows …, a diff of only these runs `full` and `web` (#5002); the case sits ahead of the `.github/` one below."
- (d) In the "Run everything but the db suites" bullet, change "anything under .github/ that is not on the skip list" to "anything under .github/ that is not on the skip list or one of those seven".
- (e) In the e2e paragraph (line 180), change `infra/, the top-level Markdown, the deploy files (the Dockerfile,` to `infra/, the top-level Markdown, the seven workflows above (#5002), the deploy files (the Dockerfile,`.

Also extend lines 188-190 so the test is said to hold `web` and `e2e` to every skip-listed file under a directory a source names. Keep `LINES=` untouched.

**4. `apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`, constants.** Below `const ENGINE = …` add:

```ts

  ".github/workflows/bot-commands.yml",

  ".github/workflows/squishy-commands.yml",
  ".github/workflows/triage.yml",

  ".github/workflows/pr-title.yml",

```

**5. `ci-scope.test.ts`, pins in `it("skips the heavy jobs for a diff of the night bot's own files and nothing else")` (lines 141-164).** Do not delete the test. Change its body as follows:

- Replace line 144 with `expect(onFor("bot/tests/test_cross.py")).toEqual([]);`.
- Delete line 145 (triage and ci-duration).
- Remove `".github/workflows/pr-title.yml",` from the list at lines 148-157. Change its comment to `// The repository's meta, which only GitHub reads (the workflows are not among it, #5002).`
- Replace line 158-159 with `// Squishy (#60): its switches.` and `expect(onFor(".squishy/config.json")).toEqual([]);`.

**6. `ci-scope.test.ts`, new tests right after that `it`.**

```ts
  // One case per file, as below: each is two script runs.
  it.each(READ_WORKFLOWS)("#5002 runs web, and nothing else, for %s, which env-production.test.ts reads", (file) => {
    expect(onFor(file), file).toEqual(["full", "web"]);
    expect(onFor("bot/harness/state.py", file), `bot + ${file}`).toEqual(["full", "web"]);
  });

  it("#5002 runs web alone for all seven together, and narrows nothing else", () => {
    expect(onFor(...READ_WORKFLOWS)).toEqual(["full", "web"]);
    expect(answerFor(".github/workflows/ci.yml", ...READ_WORKFLOWS)).toEqual(answerFor(".github/workflows/ci.yml"));
    expect(answerFor(ENGINE, ...READ_WORKFLOWS)).toEqual(answerFor(ENGINE));

```

**7. `ci-scope.test.ts`, scan helpers (the section "The paths the web's and the client's sources name").**

- (a) Replace `SKIP_DIRS` usage for the walk with a new set: `const NOT_LISTED = new Set([...SKIP_DIRS, ".git", "target"]);`.
- (b) Add `filesUnder`:

```ts
/** Every file under a directory, as repository paths. */
function filesUnder(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(join(ROOT, dir), { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const path = posix.join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) return NOT_LISTED.has(entry.name) ? [] : filesUnder(path);
    return [path];
  });
}
```

- (c) Add `skipListed`. It runs the script's own `skipped()` once, over stdin, because `spec/` and `crates/cards/` hold about 5,500 files and a throwaway repository per file would not finish:

```ts
const SKIPPED_FN = /^skipped\(\) \{\n[\s\S]*?\n\}$/m.exec(readFileSync(SCRIPT, "utf8"))?.[0];

/** The paths among `files` on scripts/ci-scope.sh's skip list, by the script's own `skipped()`. */
function skipListed(files: string[]): string[] {
  if (SKIPPED_FN === undefined) throw new Error("scripts/ci-scope.sh no longer declares `skipped() {…}` as ci-scope.test.ts reads it");
  const run = spawnSync("sh", ["-c", `${SKIPPED_FN}\nwhile IFS= read -r file; do if skipped "$file"; then echo "$file"; fi; done`], {
    input: files.join("\n"),
    encoding: "utf8",
  });
  if (run.status !== 0) throw new Error(`skipped() failed: ${run.stderr}`);
  return run.stdout.split("\n").filter((line) => line !== "");
}
```

Use `if … fi` in the loop, not `&&`, so the loop's exit status is 0.

- (d) Change `named()`'s return type to `{ path: string; dir?: string } | undefined`. Its last line becomes `return stat?.isDirectory() ? { path: `${path}/x`, dir: path } : { path };`. The other `return undefined` lines stay.
- (e) Add `noted(map, key, file)`, which does `const files = map.get(key) ?? []; if (!files.includes(file)) files.push(file); map.set(key, files);`. Rewrite `namedPaths` to return `{ paths, listed }`:
  - `paths` is the old `found`, filled with `noted(paths, hit.path, file)`.
  - `dirs` is a `Map` filled with `noted(dirs, hit.dir, file)` when `hit.dir !== undefined`.
  - After the loop, `listed` is built with `for (const [dir, sources] of dirs) for (const path of skipListed(filesUnder(dir))) for (const source of sources) noted(listed, path, source);`.
  - Give it a `type Named = { paths: Map<string, string[]>; listed: Map<string, string[]> }`.

**8. `ci-scope.test.ts`, last `describe` ("…against the paths the sources name").**

- In "finds the paths it must", use `[...WEB.paths.keys()]` and `[...E2E.paths.keys()]`. Add `".github/workflows/x"` to the WEB list.
- In the loop `for (const [line, paths] of [["web", WEB], ["e2e", E2E]] as const)`, destructure `[line, { paths, listed }]`. Keep the existing per-path `it`. Add after it:

```ts
    // #5002: a source that lists a directory may open any file in it, so a skip-listed one runs the line like a path of its own.
    for (const [path, files] of listed) {
      it(`runs ${line} for ${path}, on the skip list in a directory that ${files.join(", ")} names`, () => {
        const answer = answerFor(path);
        expect(answer.full && answer[line], `${path} is on scripts/ci-scope.sh's skip list: take it off`).toBe(true);
      });
    }
```

- Add a guard test, since today `listed` is empty:

```ts
  it("#5002 reads the skip list from the script, so a directory's skip-listed files are found", () => {
    expect(WEB.paths.get(".github/workflows/x")).toContain("apps/web/src/net/env-production.test.ts");
    expect(filesUnder(".github/workflows")).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(READ_WORKFLOWS));
    expect(skipListed(READ_WORKFLOWS)).toEqual([]);
    expect(skipListed(["bot/harness/state.py", ".github/workflows/ci.yml", "CLAUDE.md", "training/README.md", "training/history/improve.jsonl"])).toEqual([
      "bot/harness/state.py",
      "CLAUDE.md",
      "training/README.md",
    ]);
  });
```

- Also edit the file's top comment (lines 1-5) to say the scans hold a named directory's skip-listed files one by one.

## Tests

Run these from the repository root:

- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/ci-scope.test.ts`. The new tests are the seven `#5002 runs web, and nothing else, for …` cases, `#5002 runs web alone for all seven together…` and `#5002 reads the skip list from the script…`. The pins keep their old names.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/env-production.test.ts` must still pass unchanged.
- **Prove the new check fails.** Run `cp scripts/ci-scope.sh /tmp/ci-scope.sh.bak`. Re-add the four deleted lines to `skipped()` temporarily. Run the first command again. It must fail: the new `#5002 …` cases fail, the guard test fails, and the new directory check fails, naming `apps/web/src/net/env-production.test.ts` and each of the seven workflows. If it does not, the check is wrong. Then restore with `cp /tmp/ci-scope.sh.bak scripts/ci-scope.sh` and confirm `git diff --stat` lists only the two files.
- Then `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` and `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`.

## Done when

- [ ] A diff of only any one of the seven gives `full=true` and `web=true`, and `e2e`, `clippy`, `infra`, `web_promote`, the db lines and every `rust_*` line `false`.
- [ ] The pins at `:144-145`, `:155` and `:159` now expect `web`.
- [ ] A directory a source names is checked file by file for skip-listed files, and the `${path}/x` probe stays.
- [ ] With the seven back on the skip list, the directory check fails and names `env-production.test.ts` and each workflow (shown by running it).
- [ ] The header comment matches the script.
- [ ] `ci-scope.test.ts` and `env-production.test.ts` pass, and eslint and typecheck are clean.
- [ ] The harness's checks pass, in particular `cargo fmt --check`, the web tests and `cargo test --workspace` (unchanged by this work).
- [ ] No file other than the two was edited, and `.bot-plan.md` was not committed.

## Risks

- **Skipped directory case.** `continue` is essential. Without it, `.github/*` runs every job and `infra`, and the `*) on e2e` case at the bottom turns e2e on. The test at step 6 (`toEqual(["full","web"])`) catches both.
- **Cost of expansion.** Probing each file with `answerFor` would mean about 6,000 throwaway commits (`spec/` has 3,650 files, `crates/cards/` 1,891). The single-process `skipped()` probe avoids this. I ran it against the real tree: it lists the seven now, and none after the change.
- **Extraction shape.** The test depends on `skipped() {` and a column-0 `}`. If the script drops that shape, `skipListed` throws a clear error rather than passing silently.
- **Walk versus `git ls-files`.** I chose a plain `readdirSync` walk over `git ls-files`, because a missing git or a "dubious ownership" error would break the whole test file at collection time. An untracked file only matters if the skip list names it, which would be a true warning anyway.
- **Stale sentence in `ci.yml`.** Its header (lines 55-56) still says the skip list holds "the workflows that run the bot". That sits under `.github/`, which the bot may not edit.
- **Extra CI.** `rust_tools_wasm` turns on for this pull request, because the new test code adds a `readFileSync(` line under `apps/` (the acceptance.rs scan). This is expected. The script itself changing also runs everything for this one pull request.

## Open questions

None block the work. One for a person: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s header says "the workflows that run the bot" are on the skip list. Update that sentence in a later pull request by hand.
````
